name: Підготовка відкритого нападу: загроза (3)
description:
In this lesson you will learn to set up a battery for a discovered attack, by means of a threat. As you know, with a 'threat' you can think of attacking a piece, a mate threat or threatening to promote. In the examples we will look at an attack and a mate threat.

What do you have to do?

Establish a battery with a threat (attack a piece, mate threat or threat to promote). Then, gain material by performing a discovered attack.

examples.pgn: {[%csl Ge5,Re8] [#]} 1. Re2 $1 Bg3 {[%csl Ge2,Ge5,Re8][%cal Ge2e8]} 2. Bxc7+ Kxc7 3. Rxe8 *
examples.text: There are three pieces on the e-file. White, by attacking the bishop with 1.Re2, can place a fourth piece on this file and use it to set up a battery with tempo. Black is obviously not obliged to remove the bishop, but if they don't, white captures this piece on the next move. If black does remove the bishop (1...Bg3), then white has a discovered attack with 2.Bxc7+. after 2...Kxc7 3.Rxe8 white has won an exchange (a rook against a bishop or knight) and a pawn.

Also in this example we see that white can set up a discovered attack with tempo. With the white knight on f5 and the black queen on d7, there are two pieces on one diagonal. With 1.Qg4 white places a third piece on this diagonal. White threatens mate (2.Qxg7#) and sets up a battery at the same time. After 1...g6 the discovered attack 2.Nxh6+ wins a queen: 2...Kf8 3.Qxd7.

texts: Create a discovered attack by first making a threat.
